E1.evidence: Compiler output is quoted in the issue: "/usr/include/boost/bind.hpp:36:1: note: ‘#pragma message: The practice of declaring the Bind placeholders (_1, _2, ...) in the global namespace is deprecated. ...’" and "/usr/include/boost/detail/iterator.hpp:13:1: note: ‘#pragma message: This header is deprecated. Use <iterator> instead.’" when building cv_bridge/src/module.cpp on Ubuntu Jammy (https://github.com/ros-perception/vision_opencv/issues/449).

E2.evidence: The deprecated elements are used inside Boost itself, not by cv_bridge: the include chain runs from cv_bridge's `#include <boost/python.hpp>` through Boost.Python headers to boost/bind.hpp and boost/detail/iterator.hpp (issue 449). The maintainer states "This issue originates further up in boostorg/python" (https://github.com/ros-perception/vision_opencv/issues/449#issuecomment-1200502772), and the upstream report says "Some of the Boost.Python headers still use the deprecated Bind placeholders in the global namespace" (https://github.com/boostorg/python/issues/359); the maintainer adds that "these warnings arise in any packages that use the system libraries" (boostorg/python#359 comment). The warning therefore occurs for any consumer that includes boost/python.hpp from Boost 1.74, independent of any assumption between cv_bridge and Boost; Boost.Python and Boost.Bind are shipped in the same Boost release, so the deprecated use is internal to that one unit.

E3.evidence: No cross-unit operation fails; the compile-time warnings come from Boost's own headers.

E4.evidence: Compiler warnings shown in issue 449 and confirmed gone after the change: "I checked the following warnings disappear after this patch is applied." (wep21, https://github.com/ros-perception/vision_opencv/pull/478).

ineligible_reason: internal: deprecation pragma messages raised by Boost.Python 1.74 headers including deprecated Boost headers (boost/bind.hpp global placeholders, boost/detail/iterator.hpp); they appear for any consumer of boost/python.hpp and originate inside Boost (fixed upstream in Boost 1.75/1.77). The cv_bridge change (PR 478) only defines BOOST_BIND_GLOBAL_PLACEHOLDERS / BOOST_ALLOW_DEPRECATED_HEADERS for the affected Boost versions to silence them, which is also a build-level change with no interface change (step 4).
notes: Fix: PR 478 merged into vision_opencv rolling as 2df63996f37ed8fbb82740de29c06e9e8ceea4ef (backported to humble as PR 492), adding to cv_bridge/src/module.hpp `#if (BOOST_VERSION / 100 >= 1073 && BOOST_VERSION / 100 <= 1076)  // Boost 1.73 - 1.76` / `#define BOOST_BIND_GLOBAL_PLACEHOLDERS` and `#if (BOOST_VERSION / 100 == 1074)  // Boost 1.74` / `#define BOOST_ALLOW_DEPRECATED_HEADERS`. The maintainer's version analysis: the Bind placeholder deprecation "was added in 1.73 and was fixed in 1.77 by https://github.com/boostorg/python/pull/315" and the iterator header deprecation "was added in 1.74 and was fixed in 1.75 by https://github.com/boostorg/python/pull/308" (https://github.com/ros-perception/vision_opencv/issues/449#issuecomment-1243072420). A possible reading as an UPGRADE between Boost.Python (consumer) and Boost.Bind (provider) was rejected because both ship in the same Boost release and are not separately released or built; that composition is also not the one the reporter reports (cv_bridge build).
